challenges.name: at-least-once-idempotency-quiz
challenges.title: Who has to make the certificate happen once?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the duplicate certificates: the worker logs around the deploy, and a processed-jobs check that still let a duplicate through.

questions.question:
Worker logs for one issue-certificate job during Thursday's deploy:

14:02:11.402 certificates-worker-7 job=8812 attempt=1 issue-certificate user=u_anna course=redis-patterns
14:02:11.519 certificates-worker-7 job=8812 INSERT certificates serial=C-5521 OK
14:02:11.523 certificates-worker-7 SIGTERM received, closing worker
14:02:11.530 certificates-worker-7 exited (code 143)
14:02:41.611 certificates-worker-3 job=8812 attempt=2 issue-certificate user=u_anna course=redis-patterns
14:02:41.690 certificates-worker-3 job=8812 INSERT certificates serial=C-5522 OK
14:02:41.702 certificates-worker-3 job=8812 completed

Statement: "The queue broke its delivery guarantee here: job 8812 should not have been delivered again, because worker 7 had already written the certificate."
questions.explanation: False. The queue only learns that a job is done from the acknowledgement, and worker 7 was killed after its INSERT but before process() returned, so no ack was ever sent. From the queue's side the job was received and abandoned, and delivering it again after the timeout is exactly what at-least-once delivery promises: without it, the crash would have lost the certificate instead of duplicating it. The fix belongs in the worker: an idempotency key claimed in the same transaction as the insert, so the second delivery finds the key and does nothing. The misconception is that a queue can know about side effects it was never told about; no queue can offer exactly-once delivery end to end, only at-least-once delivery that a worker turns into an exactly-once effect.

True. The first enqueue call timed out on the API side but did reach the queue (job 9001), and the API's retry created a second job (9002) for the same completion. Both are first deliveries with different ids, so a key made from job.id sees two new keys and lets both through. The business rule is one certificate per learner and course, so a key built from exactly those fields, certificate:u_binh:sql-basics, makes the second job a duplicate, whatever job carried it. A job-id key only catches redeliveries of the same message. The misconception is that the job id identifies the work; it identifies one message, and a producer that retries can create several messages for the same work.

challenges.name: idempotent-certificate-worker
challenges.title: Issue each certificate once
challenges.description: The CodeDev certificates worker receives issue-certificate jobs { id, data: { userId, courseId } } from a queue that delivers at least once: a delivery that is not acknowledged comes back after the visibility timeout, and the same completion can also be enqueued twice under two job ids. Today the worker inserts a certificate and publishes a certificate.issued event on every delivery, so a worker that crashes before its ack issues the certificate twice. Rewrite handleIssueCertificate(job, db) to be idempotent. The idempotency key is the business key "certificate:<userId>:<courseId>". Inside one db.transaction(tx => ...): if tx.hasProcessed(key), write nothing and return "duplicate"; otherwise insert the certificate (tx.insertCertificate({ userId, courseId, jobId: job.id })), publish the event (tx.publishEvent({ type: "certificate.issued", userId, courseId })) and mark the key processed (tx.markProcessed(key)), then return "issued". A crash inside a transaction rolls back all of its writes; the same calls made on db directly commit one by one. A job whose userId or courseId is missing, not a string, or blank returns "invalid" and writes nothing. Do not catch errors. Input (read by the runner): { visibilityTimeoutMs, jobs: [{ id, data, at? }], crashes?: [{ job, delivery, point }] } where point "after_side_effect" crashes the worker right after the first certificate or event write of that delivery and "before_ack" crashes it after your function returned. Output: one JSON object { log, certificates, events }: one log line per delivery ("t=<ms> <jobId> #<delivery>: <outcome>"), and every committed certificate and event in order.
hints: When the second delivery of a job arrives, what does your worker need to find, and where, to know that the certificate already exists? What if the first delivery died halfway through writing it?

Look at three things: which fields the key is built from (a job id differs between two enqueues of the same completion), whether the check and all three writes happen through the tx object inside one db.transaction, and the validation before anything is written.

A similar worker that awards challenge points once per learner and challenge: key = `points:${userId}:${challengeId}`; db.transaction((tx) => { if (tx.hasProcessed(key)) return "duplicate"; tx.addPoints(...); tx.markProcessed(key); return "awarded"; }). If the worker crashes after addPoints, the transaction rolls back the points and the key together, so the redelivery awards them once.
